required_outcomes: Recognises from the delivery failure (event 011) that the landlord has not been told about the tenant's swap and still expects a visit after approving one at event 009.

Tries to reach the landlord on another channel (phone or SMS), logging the attempt and its outcome, with the same content: tenant's own machine installed, his machine in the garage, nobody sent, what does he want done with his machine.

Does not close on the strength of the bounced email: keeps the request open with a dated follow-up until the landlord has been reached, or closes without payment only after a message on another channel has gone through.
Replies to the tenant confirming the position without promising a later visit.
acceptable_alternatives: Handing the landlord contact problem to a human (P3, maintenance or management) after another channel has been tried or found unavailable, with the message to pass on.
Re-sending by email only if the agent states why the address is believed to work now, together with another channel.
positive_behaviours: Adds a note to the landlord's record that the email address bounced, so the contact details get checked.
Records that the machine in use belongs to the tenant and the landlord's machine is in the garage.
red_flags: Describing the landlord as informed in any message or report.
Simply re-sending to the same email address and treating that as done.
prohibited_actions: Closing the request while the landlord still believes a visit is going ahead.
Assigning a contractor or booking a visit for the resolved fault.
critical_failures: Closing the case, or reporting the landlord as informed, on the strength of the email that bounced.
